sections.h2: What does the Rowan County Register of Deeds office do?
sections.html:
The county describes the register's duty as the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of every public record recorded in the office. For a house seller, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the deed of trust that secures a loan both live there.

The office offers more than land records. It lists online certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, where identity is verified through an online system and a vendor adds a small convenience fee, and it serves as a passport acceptance facility. Those services help families settling an estate, who often need death certificates to support a deed or probate filing. The office also says it is committed to every citizen of the county, which in practice means the same counter serves buyers, lenders and heirs.

sections.h2: How does e-recording work in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Rowan County started electronic recording in August 2010 and accepts electronically submitted documents, maps included. The county says this helps banks, title companies, law firms and other businesses in real estate deals.

The county lists these benefits of e-recording:

  • No travel time or travel cost to reach the counter
  • No check writing, since fees are handled electronically
  • Document security
  • Real-time tracking of document status
  • A quick return of the recording information and a stamped image
  • An easy start for new users

An individual seller does not usually sign up for this. The closing attorney or title company that handles the Rowan County sale will already use a vendor from the county's vendor list.

sections.h2: How does Property Check protect a Rowan County owner?
sections.html:
It emails or texts you when a filing appears under a name or parcel number you register. The county is direct about why: the register does not decide whether a document is genuine, so a fraudulent paper that meets statutory recording requirements and has the fees paid can still enter the record.

Property Check is free, runs around the clock and sends alerts through the contact method you pick. The county admits it cannot block a bad filing, only warn you quickly. If you suspect fraud, call local law enforcement. Owners of vacant or inherited houses in Rowan County gain the most, because nobody is otherwise looking at the record. Questions on the system go to 704-216-8636.

sections.h2: How do I record a map or survey in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Have the Rowan County Review Officer sign the map first, then bring it to the register on one of three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches or 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers work in the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

You get the original back after recording, and the office keeps a digital copy. The county says to ask about electronic map recording. If your lot sits in a recorded subdivision or you hold a recorded survey, a copy costs $2 at the register's counter. Sellers sometimes order one to settle a boundary question before a buyer orders a survey.

sections.h2: What does North Carolina charge on a Rowan County deed?
sections.html:
The state sets one fee schedule for every county, so the amounts below apply in Rowan County as they do elsewhere, and the seller covers the excise tax. The statute prints these figures:

Statutory charges at the Rowan County register
ItemStatute amount
General instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages
Added pages$4.00 each
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Excise tax$1.00 for each $500 or fractional part

The tax is collected up front, ahead of recording. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and a parcel that spans two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value. The statute calls the recording fees complete and exclusive.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter when I sell?
sections.html:
A conveyance, option or long lease has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it reaches the public record of the county that holds the parcel. Time of registration sets the ranking between competing instruments.

Closing attorneys therefore hold funds until the deed is ready to go on the record. Ask yours to confirm that earlier mortgages were released and that any transfer from an heir or ex-spouse already appears in the Rowan County record.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Rowan County house?
sections.html:
A death transfer starts with the court clerk, not the register. When a small estate has no will, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk of the person's home county once 30 days have passed. The statute's limit is $20,000 of personal property, or up to $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the sole heir, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property owned.

Estates above those limits need a personal representative named by the court. After that, the paper that shows who can sign the deed is what the register records, so ask a probate attorney before listing. A buyer's title insurer will want the right authority on record, and Property Check can watch the parcel while the house sits empty.

sections.h2: What happens after a Rowan County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Tax Assessor's office updates ownership for billing, and the register's office keeps the recorded image. The Tax Assessor page lists a separate land records contact, so a new owner who does not get a tax bill should reach out there. Rowan County Tax Administration also publishes a parcel map tool for checking boundaries and parcel numbers.

For the seller, recording is the moment the deed becomes public. After that, the real work is the tax proration at closing and any bill for the year that arrives in the buyer's name. The county's tax pages describe the assessor's job as listing, assessing and billing all taxable property, so the register and assessor each handle half of the paper trail.

sections.h2: What should a Rowan County seller check at the register before listing?
sections.html:
Pull the recorded deed that put the property in your name, then confirm that the names, the legal description and the parcel number match your sale contract. Rowan County offers an online document search for land records, so you can check this before you call anyone.

  • Search for the vesting deed and read the names exactly as recorded.
  • Look for each deed of trust and confirm a satisfaction was recorded after payoff.
  • Check for easements, rights of way or an old recorded map that affects the lot.
  • Sign up for Property Check if the house will sit empty during the sale.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed will go in by e-recording or by hand.

Fix problems early. A gap such as a deed from a deceased owner or an unreleased lien can add weeks to a closing, and cash buyers value a clean record as much as any other buyer.

faqs.q: When did Rowan County start electronic recording?
faqs.a: The Rowan County Register of Deeds began electronic recording in August 2010, and the office accepts electronically submitted documents including maps.
Yes. You create an account, list a name or parcel number and choose how to be alerted when a filing is recorded.

faqs.q: Which map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?
faqs.a: The county accepts 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches. The Rowan County Review Officer must sign before the map goes to the register.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Rowan County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, as transferor, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded survey cost?
faqs.a: The county says a copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.
